question: Do event features improve the H3 zone-hour forecast (with vs without)?
note: Trips are real (Citi Bike JC). News input is the curated fixture corpus (data/fixtures/news_eval_combined.jsonl, 14 articles -> 5 extracted events), not live news. Metrics are from executed fits only.

runs.name: event_at_test_boundary
runs.finding: Structural zero: with the only events at the test boundary, every event feature is 0 throughout the training window (availability rule, section 5.2), so the tree model never learns a split on them and B4 predictions are bit-identical to B1.

runs.name: events_in_train_and_test
runs.news: news_eval_combined.jsonl; train window holds the 06-12 PATH failure and 06-14 concert, test window holds the 06-20 street closure and the 07-12 PATH failure + concert
runs.finding: Measured null (slightly negative): event features change the predictions (mean |B4-B1| = 0.076 departures/hour) but do not improve accuracy — test WAPE 0.5091 (B1) vs 0.5105 (B3/B4), event-window WAPE 0.4981 vs 0.4996. Five events over three months are too sparse at H3 zone-hour grain; the signal drowns in noise. Consistent with the V2-03 root-cause analysis: a dense structured feed lifts the forecast (+2.69% at borough grain), sparse news-derived events do not.
